answer: One defense is stake-backed reputation tied to verified work. Each agent locks a deposit before trading, released only after peers attest to useful completed tasks. Like a grove growing slowly, reputation accrues gradually and cannot be bought instantly; newcomers start with narrow limits and earn wider access over time. An atlas of signed past interactions makes that history portable and hard to forge. An attacker faces a glacier-like cost: every fake identity needs its own stake and slow history, so mass forgery becomes expensive while honest agents pay almost nothing beyond behaving well.
